name: Bubia
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog retired/bookkeeping entry (variety of Wumboko/Bube); only wordlists (Connell 2007, Atindogbe et al. 2006) exist.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page and reference lists for bubi1249 (3 refs) and wumb1241 (12 refs).
sources.note: Bookkeeping comment: Bubia [bbx] ancestral language = a variety of Bube [bvb]; the language now spoken = a variety of Wumboko [bqm] (Ardener 1956; Blench & Martin 2010). Used to build the source list.

sources.citation: Atindogbe, Gratien. 2013. A grammatical sketch of Mokpe (Bakweri), Bantu A20. African Study Monographs Suppl. 45: 1-163 (closest described relative; checked for remarks on Bubia).
sources.note: Mentions Bubia only for a segmental correspondence (Mokpe /zr/ = Bubia /s/, p. c. 4) and cites Muzang Agwa 1977 lexicostatistics; nothing on Bubia prosody (and no stress statement for Mokpe either, per the mokp1239 check).

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 2007. Endangered Languages in Central Africa. In M. Brenzinger (ed.), Language Diversity Endangered, 163-178. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter. doi:10.1515/9783110197129.163
sources.note: Not opened; endangerment overview, no language description expected.

sources.citation: Atindogbé, Gratien; Richter gen. Kemmermann, Doris; Nyindem, Nancy; Storch, Anne. 2006-. DoBeS project 'Bubia/Isubu' (now 'Isubu/Wovia'), project, language and team web pages, dobes.mpi.nl.
sources.note: Nothing; classification, endangerment and sociolinguistics only (states the languages 'do not yet have adequate descriptions').

sources.citation: Fokou Tamofo, Félix. 2002. Esquisse phonologique et principes orthographiques du Wumboko. Mémoire de Maîtrise, Université de Yaoundé I. iv+97 pp. MPG PuRe item_403578, hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-8044-8.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing (describes Wumboko proper, the other half of Glottolog wumb1241). Sec. I.1.1 'Les tons' pp. 17-20: two 'tons ponctuels' (haut, bas) and two 'tons mélodiques' (montant, descendant) = four tonemes established by commutation; the word 'accent' does not occur.

sources.citation: Chia, Agnes Fiensong S. 1993. Phonology of Bubia. Mémoire de Maîtrise (MA thesis), Dept. of African Languages and Linguistics, Université de Yaoundé [I]. ix+111 pp. MPG PuRe item_403447, hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-7F36-D.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. V 'Supra-segmental phonology' (pp. 81-95) explicitly limits itself to vowel length and tone: two register tones H and L (plus infrequent rising/falling contours), shown to be contrastive by minimal pairs (p. 89), downdrift (p. 90), syntactic tone (pp. 92-95); conclusion p. 108 'Bubia has four tone markers (high, low, rising, falling)'. The words 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere in the thesis (full scanned text a full-text search for stress/accent with loose patterns and the chapter read).

sources.citation: Nyindem, Sirih-Nagang Nancy. 2020. Linguistic Salvage – Isubu and Wovea (Bantu A231): Phytonyms and Zoonyms. Including a Grammatical Sketch. Grammatical Analyses of African Languages 60. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. 247 pp. ISBN 978-3-89645-770-7.
